LESSON: READING 4.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.2: Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why are pictures important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. create mental images from text they have viewed, read or heard
2. answer factual and inferential questions correctly

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 4.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: COMPREHENSION
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 4.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: COMPREHENSION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Create mental images from text they have viewed, read or heard

What this means
In this part you learn to create mental images from text they have viewed, read or heard. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create mental images from text they have viewed, read or heard.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create mental images from text they have viewed, read or heard. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Answer factual and inferential questions correctly

What this means
In this part you learn to answer factual and inferential questions correctly. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: answer factual and inferential questions correctly.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can answer factual and inferential questions correctly. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: create mental images from text they have viewed, read or heard)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension to a partner. (skill: answer factual and inferential questions correctly)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: create mental images from text they have viewed, read or heard.
3. Practise this skill: answer factual and inferential questions correctly.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why are pictures important?
2. How can you use pictures to communicate ?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: create mental images from text they have viewed, read or heard.
5. Be able to: answer factual and inferential questions correctly.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
